overall: The AG found the School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate March 5, 2026 minutes that recorded a unanimous vote when one member had left, but found no violation on the public-comment minutes and deemed the May 14 amendment adequate remediation.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the March 5, 2026 meeting recorded a unanimous vote to approve prior minutes, though one member listed as present had left and did not vote.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate minutes of the March 5, 2026, meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes did not sufficiently describe an interaction during the public comment period at the March 5, 2026 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We reiterate that meeting minutes need not be a transcript of the remarks and a public body is not required to capture every comment made during public comment in order to substantially comply with the accuracy requirement of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further remedial action ordered because the Committee amended the minutes to reflect the vote as it occurred on May 14, 2026).
remedy_passage: We do order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
